description: Curated CNS-relevant drugs annotated with BBB permeability and the BBB transporter targets they interact with. Mechanism = how the drug crosses (or fails to cross) the BBB.

high.label: High BBB permeability
high.description: Crosses readily, free CNS exposure ≥ plasma.

moderate.label: Moderate
moderate.description: Limited CNS exposure; usually still therapeutic.

low.label: Low / restricted
low.description: Largely excluded — efflux substrate or polarity barrier.

carrier.label: Carrier-mediated
carrier.description: Crosses via a specific transporter (SLC, RMT).

biologic.label: Biologic — engineered
biologic.description: Antibody/protein therapeutic engineered for RMT-mediated transcytosis.

drugs.name: Levodopa
drugs.mechanism: Influx via LAT1 (SLC7A5/SLC3A2). Co-administered with carbidopa to prevent peripheral decarboxylation.

drugs.name: Gabapentin
drugs.mechanism: LAT1 substrate at the BBB.

drugs.name: Melphalan
drugs.mechanism: Phenylalanine mustard transported by LAT1.

drugs.name: Methotrexate
drugs.mechanism: OAT3/MRP-mediated efflux limits CNS levels; intrathecal dosing required for CNS leukemia.

drugs.name: Loperamide
drugs.mechanism: Strong P-gp substrate — actively pumped out, hence no central opioid effect at therapeutic doses.

drugs.name: Domperidone
drugs.mechanism: P-gp substrate — peripheral antiemetic without extrapyramidal effects.

drugs.name: Paclitaxel
drugs.mechanism: Dual P-gp / BCRP substrate. Limits utility for brain metastases.

drugs.name: Imatinib
drugs.mechanism: Effluxed by P-gp and BCRP; CNS exposure limited.

drugs.name: Vinblastine
drugs.mechanism: Classical P-gp substrate.

drugs.name: Digoxin
drugs.mechanism: P-gp substrate; CNS exclusion is therapeutically desirable.

drugs.name: Verapamil
drugs.mechanism: P-gp inhibitor + substrate; widely used as PET tracer for P-gp function.

drugs.name: Diazepam
drugs.mechanism: Lipophilic; passive transcellular diffusion.

drugs.name: Caffeine
drugs.mechanism: Passive diffusion; small lipophilic xanthine.

drugs.name: Morphine
drugs.mechanism: Weak P-gp substrate; CNS levels tempered by efflux.

drugs.name: Risperidone
drugs.mechanism: P-gp substrate but enough crosses for therapeutic effect.

drugs.name: Phenytoin
drugs.mechanism: Modest P-gp substrate; readily crosses BBB.

drugs.name: Methylphenidate
drugs.mechanism: Lipophilic; crosses passively.

drugs.name: Donanemab
drugs.mechanism: IgG1 mAb. ~0.1% reaches brain by passive paracellular leak / minimal transcytosis.

drugs.name: Lecanemab
drugs.mechanism: Humanized IgG1 mAb. CNS penetration ~0.1–0.3% of plasma.

drugs.name: Trontinemab
drugs.mechanism: Anti-Aβ mAb fused to a monovalent low-affinity TfR1 binder (Brain Shuttle); 5–10× brain penetration.

drugs.name: Etranacogene dezaparvovec
drugs.mechanism: AAV5; does NOT efficiently cross intact BBB. Listed for contrast.

drugs.name: Idursulfase-IT
drugs.mechanism: Direct intrathecal delivery — bypasses BBB entirely (failed RMT efforts).

drugs.name: Aducanumab
drugs.mechanism: Anti-Aβ IgG1; ~0.1% CNS penetration.

drugs.name: Galactose
drugs.mechanism: GLUT1-mediated; same transporter as glucose.

drugs.name: L-Phenylalanine
drugs.mechanism: LAT1 substrate; competitor of L-DOPA.

drugs.name: Cyclosporine A
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits P-gp at high doses — used to chemosensitize the BBB.

drugs.name: Tariquidar
drugs.mechanism: Third-generation efflux inhibitor.

drugs.name: Mannitol
drugs.mechanism: Hyperosmotic; transiently opens tight junctions (Doolittle protocol for chemotherapy delivery).

drugs.name: Reolysin / oncolytic virus
drugs.mechanism: Convection-enhanced delivery (intratumoral) bypassing BBB.

drugs.name: Methadone
drugs.mechanism: P-gp substrate; CNS levels variable across genotypes.

drugs.name: Topotecan
drugs.mechanism: BCRP substrate — restricts brain entry.

drugs.name: Sumatriptan
drugs.mechanism: Polar; limited BBB crossing — peripheral 5HT1B/D action sufficient.

drugs.name: Lamivudine
drugs.mechanism: Active OAT3-mediated efflux out of CNS.

drugs.name: Zidovudine (AZT)
drugs.mechanism: Limited BBB penetration; OAT3 efflux.

drugs.name: Ivermectin
drugs.mechanism: P-gp substrate — toxicity in P-gp-deficient collies illustrates CNS exclusion.
